Subject: Initial AWS offer page draft and co-sell ask

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the POC. We reviewed the feature set and our GTM leads want to move this to AWS Marketplace as a co-sell offer. I attached a first-pass product description that our marketing team filled out — they asked us to run it by your listing owner to make sure the technical claims and pricing align with Redwood's approved wording.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm transactable pricing model: meter vs. SaaS subscription (we prefer subscription).
- Short product blurb (1-3 lines) that can be used on the Marketplace hero card.
- Confirmation that the architecture diagram accurately represents data flow to the customer's VPC.
- Co-sell manifest: do you have a standard statement we can include for the AWS partner scoring?

Attachments: aws_offer_page_v1.docx (draft copy), product_arch_diagram.png

If helpful we can join a 30m sync with your marketplace person and our procurement lead (procurements@cloudinsight.com) later this week.

Best,
Emily
Emily Roberts
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudInsight

Subject: Re: Initial AWS offer page draft and co-sell ask

Emily — thanks for the draft. Adding Marissa and Marcus from our GTM and product pages teams to align on copy and pricing.

Quick answers up front:
- We generally prefer a transactable SaaS subscription model on AWS Marketplace for products with ongoing infra costs; we'll propose a monthly subscription SKU.
- I'll attach our suggested short blurb and a trimmed hero line for the offer card.
- The diagram looks close; Marcus can confirm the VPC details.
- We do have a standard co-sell statement but need to confirm with AWS enablement on the exact language that maps to their scoring rubric.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to provide a revised hero + 1-paragraph product summary.
2) Marcus to validate/annotate the architecture diagram.
3) I'll coordinate with AWS Marketplace Enablement for the co-sell manifest and confirm listing type.
4) If agreed, schedule a 30m sync Thurs 07/22 10:30am ET — please confirm.

Attachments: aws_offer_page_v1.docx (updated with our comments), co-sell_manifest.pdf (placeholder)

Thanks,
Priyom

Subject: Re: Initial AWS offer page draft and co-sell ask

Thanks — I took a pass on the hero and the short paragraph. Inline comments are in the attached doc, but high level:

Hero (one-liner for hero card):
"Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference platform with predictable cost controls and enterprise-grade routing across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Short product summary (1 paragraph):
"Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime to serve large language models with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Built-in smart routing, KV caching, and model quantization allow engineering teams to deploy production-grade generative features while controlling unit economics and meeting regulatory requirements."

Pricing recommendation (internal):
- Primary: Monthly subscription (metering optional add-on)
- Suggested SKU tiers: dev (limited tokens), standard, enterprise (dedicated capacity + SLA)

I've also left an edit requesting we avoid the term 'serverless' on the marketplace page — it complicates the expected billing model. Marcus — please see page 3 of the doc for architecture notes.

Attachments: aws_offer_page_v1.docx (marissa_v1)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Marketing, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: AWS Marketplace Enablement <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, Emily Roberts <emily.roberts@cloudinsight.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial AWS offer page draft and co-sell ask

Looping in some marketplace packaging notes — quick checklist before we request enablement to kick:

- Confirm whether offer will be transactable by AWS (SaaS subscription) vs. listing only. If transactable, legal needs to sign the AWS Marketplace Seller Agreement — I can share the DocuSign once you confirm.
- AWS requires a 1-line short description (<=140 chars) + 3 feature bullets for the hero. We should supply localized copy for US and EU.
- Co-sell: to qualify for the AWS co-sell program we need an explicit go-to-market plan and a filled co-sell manifest (template attached). Make sure to include expected ARR motions and a couple of joint customer target logos.
- Branding: use the AWS-approved partner badge; do not include AWS logos in product screenshots. Marketing will handle the badge placement.
- Security artifacts: AWS Marketplace enablement usually requests SOC 2 type II and data flow docs; have Marcus confirm which docs we can surface publicly vs. in the secure bundle.

Proposal: Priyom, if you confirm the Thursday sync we can invite the AWS Enablement rep and CloudInsight procurement so we can finalize whether this will be a transactable SaaS offer. I can bring the DocuSign to that meeting so legal signoff is quick.

Forwarded message:
> On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 11:18 AM marissa_cole@redwood.ai wrote:
> > (see attached edits and hero text)
> >
> > -- Marissa

Attachments: co-sell_manifest.pdf, aws_offer_page_v1.docx (marissa_v1), product_arch_diagram.png

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
